summary.title: Be Kind
summary.one_liner: Kindness at work means taking responsibility for your impact on others, and it makes you more effective, not less, as the author learned after nearly being sidelined at Facebook for being hard to work with.
keywords: being right vs working well with others
takeaways: Being kind means taking responsibility for how your presence affects the people around you, not just being nice or giving superficial praise.
Being right is not the same as being valuable; if colleagues avoid working with you, your impact is limited.
Kindness does not require diluting your opinions or the passion with which you present them.
Being considerate of colleagues' feelings tends to get you invited into more conversations, which scales your impact.
The author describes this as a long-term strategy for maximizing impact, while admitting he still slips back into old habits under stress.
summary.summary: This personal essay by Boz, an early Facebook engineer, recounts how he was almost removed from News Feed after colleagues described him as hard to work with despite his technical skill. He reflects that he had treated being right as his main job, and that his partner's feedback to "be kind" changed his career. The post separates kindness from niceness and defines it as taking responsibility for your impact on others. It argues that kindness has not reduced his effectiveness and has instead increased his influence. The essay is short and anecdotal, with no code or formal technique.
